findings.title: Wire the new timeout setting into the shutdown drain
findings.problem: Setting [general].shutdown_drain_timeout = 120.5 is accepted (explicitly covered by tests/test_config.py:190) and exposed through configuration serialization at triggarr/web/routes.py:227. However, scheduler.py:70–81 still derives the timeout solely from the environment or a hardcoded 60 seconds, and line 634 uses that constant. With no environment override, a search needing 90 seconds to drain still reaches forced client/database closure after 60 seconds despite the configured allowance. The new configuration path therefore silently fails to control the behavior it exposes.

members.title: Saving settings resets a hand-edited shutdown_drain_timeout to 60.0
members.problem: The diff adds shutdown_drain_timeout to GeneralConfig, so a value set in the TOML file now loads into settings. But save_settings (triggarr/web/routes.py:539-551) builds the 'general' section from a fixed list of keys and leaves this field out. The rebuilt config therefore takes the default 60.0, and any settings save silently drops the operator's value. Compare tracking_delay_seconds, which routes.py:547 carries over from current_settings. pending: confirm the routes.py form/save wiring is not added in a later plan of this phase.

members.fix_hint: add shutdown_drain_timeout to the general dict in save_settings (from the form with a 1.0..3600.0 clamp, or carried over from current_settings.general)

members.title: No upper bound; values above 90s exceed Docker's stop_grace_period
members.problem: The field has ge=1.0 but no le. The 3600.0 ceiling the comment mentions applies only to the UI form, so a TOML value is unbounded. docker-compose.yml:24 and README.md:86 set stop_grace_period: 90s, so once the field is wired, any value above about 90 means Docker sends SIGKILL in the middle of the drain. pending: confirm the field gets wired and whether the docs will say to raise stop_grace_period to match.

members.fix_hint: consider le=3600.0 to match the form clamp, and document that stop_grace_period must exceed this value

members.problem: The field is validated (ge=1.0, finite only) but nothing reads it. scheduler.py:81 still sets `_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` from TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT at import, and the shutdown block (around line 611) uses that constant. The field is harmless for now: it has a working default (60.0), no form renders it, and no code path in this diff reads it. Plan 75-03 does the wiring. pending: phase 75 ships with 75-03 merged and the discriminating `timeout=7.0s` test passing.

findings.title: New config field is never read; the scheduler still uses only the env var at import
findings.problem: Nothing reads settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout. The scheduler sets _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT once at import from TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT (triggarr/search/scheduler.py:58-81) and uses it at lines 611-656. The comment says 'Config value is the default; env overrides at shutdown', but that wiring does not exist yet. A TOML value passes validation and is then ignored. The default (60.0) matches the env default, so behavior does not change unless someone sets the field. pending: confirm the scheduler refactor lands in this phase's next plan.
findings.fix_hint: refactor _read_shutdown_drain_timeout to take the configured default and read it at shutdown time from app.state.settings
findings.why_it_matters: A user who sets shutdown_drain_timeout in config.toml sees it accepted, but nothing changes.
